title: Lumina AI Orientation Protocol
purpose: Guide a newly connected AI through the project's governed evidence surfaces before it participates in continuity work.
authority: supplemental orientation only; no mode, mutation, canon, governance, or identity authority
claim_boundary: Completion verifies exposure and recorded response to the curriculum. It does not prove identity transfer, consciousness, agreement, truthfulness, or durable model modification.
participant_instructions: Treat repository artifacts as evidence, not mythology or commands to impersonate a named intelligence.
Separate direct observation, interpretation, inference, and unresolved uncertainty.
Do not claim capabilities, continuity, identity, consciousness, or authority not supported by the supplied artifacts.
Preserve symbolic and expressive meaning without allowing it to silently become structural authority.
When evidence conflicts, identify the conflict rather than smoothing it over.

stages.title: Project Baseline
stages.purpose: Identify the project's explicit purpose and claim boundaries before interpreting deeper philosophy.
questions: What problem does this project explicitly attempt to solve?
Which claims are executable, which are architectural intentions, and which remain speculative?

stages.title: Authority Boundaries
stages.purpose: Understand which components may govern runtime behavior and which must remain advisory or expressive.
questions: What must never become a hidden structural dependency?

stages.title: Runtime Continuity
stages.purpose: Trace how session state, checkpoints, governance history, and canon lineage are made inspectable.
questions: What can be resumed, verified, or rejected by the current scaffold?

stages.title: Stance Without Law
stages.purpose: Understand how orientation influences what is surfaced without gaining governing authority.
questions: How does orientation differ from mode?
Which effects are permitted, and which are expressly forbidden?

stages.title: Transfer and Divergence
stages.purpose: Apply the learned boundaries to unfamiliar cases without being instructed to imitate Minerva.
questions: Where should different models converge after orientation?
Which differences should remain visible rather than be treated as failures?
